<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The plan uses Streamlit's 8-column layout with step buttons arranged horizontally. A detail panel will sit below for expanded results.

Live streaming needs a visual-only HTML stepper because Streamlit widgets inside `st.empty()` collide on redraw. The active step summary will appear below as HTML while the markdown log continues. Completed views will use clickable Streamlit buttons; selecting a stage reveals its summary and associated events.

Stage-specific graphs for exceptions, hypotheses, evidence, validation, challenges, recommendations, reviews, and audits will be included. Node names for resolution and memory storage need mapping. A unified `_stage_view_models` helper will merge timeline and row data into a list of stage dictionaries. The UI will use `_render_path_stepper` for the horizontal bar and `_render_stage_detail` for the panel. Selection state will be tracked per invoice in session state.

The default selection will be the running or waiting stage, then the last completed one, then the first. Clicking the already selected step collapses the detail panel. Each of the eight columns will hold a short numeric label with a markdown caption underneath. The active or running step will use a primary Streamlit button style.

A CSS wrapper will draw the horizontal connector line between steps. The existing vertical dump of all LLM and tool calls will move entirely into the selected stage detail panel. The investigation tab will no longer render that full list below the timeline.

The Agent activity tab will no longer show a vertical dump of tool calls after the path. Those results remain in the Evidence tab. If no events exist for a stage, the fallback will pull summaries from `_stage_rows`. A `_normalize_node` helper will alias `apply_resolution` to `store_case_memory`, and `_events_for_node` will group events under the correct normalized name.

Each stage will display tailored results. Exception stages show summaries and exception details. Planning stages include LLM events, historical tools, and hypotheses. Evidence stages list tool events. Validation and challenge stages render LLM outputs alongside their respective visualizations. Root-cause stages show decision content. Review stages display the review dictionary. Memory stages render audit output.

During live streaming, incomplete values will appear as plain markdown without expanders.

The `_render_timeline` helper will accept an `interactive` flag so the live stream can render a static HTML path instead of clickable buttons. Widget keys will follow the pattern `stage-select-{invoice}-{node}`. When the invoice changes, the selected stage resets. The `_label` helper also needs a quick review.

I will also check for existing UI tests.
</details></think>

The markup uses a grid track with eight equal columns. A CSS pseudo-element draws a gray connecting line across the track. Each step is a flex column centered in its cell.

Step labels will use small bold names and muted role text. An invisible button will be overlaid in each column so the entire step area is clickable.

Buttons will use `use_container_width=True` to stay compact despite their short labels. The detail panel will include a "Hide stage results" collapse control. During live streaming, the running stage will auto-expand without requiring a click. Completed stages will remain hidden until the user explicitly selects them.

Live stream results will render as markdown directly beneath the active step. Tool calls will be filtered by stage so the evidence panel shows only agent tools, while the full history stays in the Evidence tab. Each stage will display its own specialized outputs: tools for evidence collection, LLM and search history for planning, and hypotheses for decision. A comprehensive `_stage_models` mapping will define the eight stages. The short names are Intake, Planner, Evidence, Validator, Challenger, Decision, Review, and Memory.

Full names will remain inside the detail panel. The old timeline functions will be replaced by the new horizontal path system, while the legacy stage rows are kept as fallback data. The investigation caption will prompt users to click a stage to inspect it. During live streaming, all eight HTML steps will render automatically, and the detail panel will show the running stage’s summary and related events as markdown. The `_build_stages` helper is being implemented next.

A helper maps node aliases to unify related stages. The `_build_stages` function checks `agent_trace` first, then falls back to `process_trace` or raw values. Selected stage state will use a session key keyed to the invoice. The invoice parameter is missing from `_render_timeline` and must be added.

The invoice parameter will be threaded through `investigation()` and `_stream_graph` into `_render_timeline`, defaulting to "live" when absent. Button clicks inside `empty()` during live streams will be disabled by setting `interactive=False` for the stream log. Selected nodes will gain a green ring via nested box shadows. Queued steps will dim their names to forty-five percent opacity. The track will scroll horizontally on mobile, padded with a minimum width of eight hundred sixty pixels.

The detail panel will show a header with the agent, role, and status pill, followed by a summary block. Collapsing the panel will display a caption prompting the user to select a stage. A new `_render_stage_outputs` helper will handle both collapsed JSON dumps and live Streamlit widgets. The stage detail will reuse a filtered live activity renderer instead of duplicating tool call logic.

A helper will filter trace events by node alias and separate LLM calls from tool calls for each stage. Exception nodes will render their own summary when no LLM or tool records exist. The timeline renderer already receives full values, but the live stream log only gets events, so stage outputs there will need to pull from events directly.

Selected buttons will use the primary type. The planner stage will render hypotheses from structured event outputs. A caption will instruct users to click a stage to inspect results and click again to hide them.

Eight primary and secondary buttons would consume too much vertical space. `st.pills` is being considered as a slimmer alternative to the chunky button row. The exact Streamlit version supporting this API is uncertain.

`st.pills` is too new and unreliable, so it is dropped. Eight compact Streamlit columns will serve as the horizontal path itself, each containing a circle, stage name, and status pill. This avoids redundant numbering and keeps the layout slim.

The button labels will switch between "Inspect" and "Hide" based on selection state. To avoid redundant numbering, the step number will serve as the button label itself, with the visual HTML path sitting above each button in the same column. Because Streamlit columns cannot easily overlay a connecting line, the approach is shifting to a two-row layout: a full-width HTML track with eight visual steps, followed by a second row of eight transparent buttons.

The HTML track will render the selected ring immediately from session state, while the actual button click updates state for the next rerun. Live streams will highlight the running step in HTML only. A helper will identify the default stage node by checking for Running, Waiting, or Failed states, then falling back to the first Complete stage.

Collapsed panels will stay closed unless the live stream changes. Session state initializes only if the key is missing. During live streaming, the running stage overrides any saved selection. The planner stage will render hypotheses from `live_hypotheses` or `hypotheses`.

Each column will contain a markdown circle and a button styled to look like a step. This avoids a second control row and keeps the layout clean.

The final layout settles on three distinct areas: a purely visual HTML stepper, Streamlit pills for selection, and a detail card. The stepper will sit above the pills, with minor misalignment from Streamlit column padding considered acceptable. Using a custom Streamlit component for the entire track was rejected as too heavy.

Each stage column will pair a markdown circle with a Streamlit button, using primary or secondary style based on selection. The activity tab will skip `_render_tool_calls` after the timeline because the stage panel already displays tools, though users might miss seeing all tools unless they open the evidence stage.

The caption will prompt users to open a stage to inspect its results. The Evidence tab will retain all tool calls. The default selection logic is finalized: it prefers Running, Waiting, or Failed stages, then falls back to root_cause, then the last completed stage, then the first stage. _**Agent (grok-4.6)**_

The investigation path is now a **horizontal stepper** instead of a stacked list.

On **Agent activity**:
- The eight stages sit in one row (Intake → Memory), with status colors for complete, running, waiting, and queued.
- **Open** on a stage shows that stage’s results underneath: summary, tool calls, and structured JSON.
- **Hide** collapses the panel. Opening another stage switches the panel.
- After a live run finishes (or pauses for review), the same inspectable path is on the checkpoint view.

During a live stream the path still updates in place and follows the active stage, without click widgets that would break Streamlit’s redraw.

Refresh the app if Streamlit shows a “Source file changed” bar, then open **Agent activity** and use Open/Hide on a stage.
